text: What you took for the last outcrop of the fen turns its head.
Moss has had a long time with him. Out of his shoulders and all down his back the stone has grown red crystal, and the same red is banked in his eyes.
"No," he says. The word arrives slowly, the way weather does.

choices.text: I have not asked you anything yet.
Step back from the fen the way you came.

text: Goor has not moved. The fire on the columns has burned down a hand's width and been fed by nobody.
He settles a fraction, which on something that size is the whole of a shrug.
"I am Goor. I stand here. That is the arrangement."
"A whole new realm," says Goor, and for a moment the crystals on his back come up brighter, as if the ring had answered him.
"Not more of this. Not another fen with another wood behind it. Green over green over green, and rain that never reaches the floor, and things down there that have never once seen the open."
"It is not shut because it is empty. It is shut because it is not."

choices.text: Look at it a while longer.

text: "The ones who cut the ring. They went through."
A long pause. Somewhere under the moss, something settles.
"They did not come back out. So: no."
"I have stood here through two floods and a wood. Come back when the light in it changes. You will know - so will everything in the fen."
He turns his face back to the gate, and is an outcrop again.
